translations.inspector.instrument.applied-to-every-no: applied to every note written under it
translations.inspector.instrument.da-reads-past-the: {$START_TAG_CODE}$DA ${$WRITTEN_HEX}{$CLOSE_TAG_CODE} reads past the driver's 20-entry instrument table. Where it lands depends on how that driver indexes the table, which is not something this editor can read, so the bytes it picks up are not shown. Percussion is not reached this way — that is {$START_TAG_CODE}@21{$CLOSE_TAG_CODE}–{$START_TAG_CODE}@29{$CLOSE_TAG_CODE}, which rewrite the note instead.
translations.inspector.instrument.da-which-reads-past: $DA ${$written}, which reads past the driver’s table
translations.inspector.instrument.does-not-help-the: {$START_TAG_CODE}@@{$WRITTEN}{$CLOSE_TAG_CODE} does not help: the direct form is remapped to {$START_TAG_CODE}@{$REMAPPED}{$CLOSE_TAG_CODE}, a custom instrument. Only a raw {$START_TAG_CODE}$DA ${$WRITTEN_HEX}{$CLOSE_TAG_CODE} reaches the driver's own entry.
translations.inspector.instrument.emits-nothing-addmu: {$START_TAG_CODE}@{$WRITTEN}{$CLOSE_TAG_CODE} emits nothing. AddmusicK writes a {$START_TAG_CODE}$DA{$CLOSE_TAG_CODE} only for {$START_TAG_CODE}@0{$CLOSE_TAG_CODE}–{$START_TAG_CODE}@18{$CLOSE_TAG_CODE} and {$START_TAG_CODE}@30{$CLOSE_TAG_CODE} upward, so the sound does not change — the channel keeps whatever instrument it already had, or instrument 0 if none was ever set. That is why it appears to be the same as {$START_TAG_CODE}@0{$CLOSE_TAG_CODE}.
translations.inspector.instrument.instrument.label: Instrument
translations.inspector.instrument.it-is-not-inert: It is not inert, though. It still records itself as the channel's instrument, which cancels a pending {$START_TAG_CODE}@21{$CLOSE_TAG_CODE}–{$START_TAG_CODE}@29{$CLOSE_TAG_CODE} drum and clears the current instrument's built-in transposition. So {$START_TAG_CODE}@2 c4 @19 c4{$CLOSE_TAG_CODE} plays one timbre at two different pitches.
translations.inspector.instrument.its-srcn-is-fixed-o: its SRCN is fixed once the song compiles
translations.inspector.instrument.no-number-given-so: No number given, so this changes nothing.
translations.inspector.instrument.not-in-the-drivers-: not in the driver’s default set
translations.inspector.instrument.past-the-end-of-thi: past the end of this song’s sample list
translations.inspector.instrument.the-direct-form-for: The direct form. For {$START_TAG_CODE}@0{$CLOSE_TAG_CODE}–{$START_TAG_CODE}@18{$CLOSE_TAG_CODE} it does exactly what the plain form does.
translations.inspector.instrument.the-direct-form-rem: The direct form remaps 19–29 to custom instruments, so it cannot write a drum.
translations.inspector.instrument.the-pitch-you-write: The pitch you write is discarded — {$START_TAG_CODE}@{$WRITTEN} c4{$CLOSE_TAG_CODE} and {$START_TAG_CODE}@{$WRITTEN} g4{$CLOSE_TAG_CODE} are the same drum at the same pitch, and only the length differs. It applies to the next note only, then the channel reverts.
translations.inspector.instrument.this-entry-is-unfin: This entry is unfinished. Each one needs a sample and five {$START_TAG_CODE}$xx{$CLOSE_TAG_CODE} bytes.
translations.inspector.instrument.undefined.am4-none: Under {$START_TAG_CODE}#am4{$CLOSE_TAG_CODE}, {$START_TAG_CODE}$DA ${$WRITTEN_HEX}{$CLOSE_TAG_CODE} means {$START_TAG_CODE}@{$REMAPPED}{$CLOSE_TAG_CODE}, a custom instrument — this song defines none. Add an {$START_TAG_CODE}#instruments{$CLOSE_TAG_CODE} block; its first entry is {$START_TAG_CODE}@30{$CLOSE_TAG_CODE}.
translations.inspector.instrument.undefined.am4-some: Under {$START_TAG_CODE}#am4{$CLOSE_TAG_CODE}, {$START_TAG_CODE}$DA ${$WRITTEN_HEX}{$CLOSE_TAG_CODE} means {$START_TAG_CODE}@{$REMAPPED}{$CLOSE_TAG_CODE}, a custom instrument — this song defines {$DEFINED}, so the highest is {$START_TAG_CODE}@{$HIGHEST}{$CLOSE_TAG_CODE}.
translations.inspector.instrument.undefined.direct-no: The direct form {$START_TAG_CODE}@@{$WRITTEN}{$CLOSE_TAG_CODE} is remapped to {$START_TAG_CODE}@{$REMAPPED}{$CLOSE_TAG_CODE}, a custom instrument — this song defines none. Add an {$START_TAG_CODE}#instruments{$CLOSE_TAG_CODE} block; its first entry is {$START_TAG_CODE}@30{$CLOSE_TAG_CODE}.
translations.inspector.instrument.undefined.direct-so: The direct form {$START_TAG_CODE}@@{$WRITTEN}{$CLOSE_TAG_CODE} is remapped to {$START_TAG_CODE}@{$REMAPPED}{$CLOSE_TAG_CODE}, a custom instrument — this song defines {$DEFINED}, so the highest is {$START_TAG_CODE}@{$HIGHEST}{$CLOSE_TAG_CODE}.
translations.inspector.instrument.undefined.plain-non: {$START_TAG_CODE}@{$WRITTEN}{$CLOSE_TAG_CODE} is a custom instrument, but this song defines none. Add an {$START_TAG_CODE}#instruments{$CLOSE_TAG_CODE} block; its first entry is {$START_TAG_CODE}@30{$CLOSE_TAG_CODE}.
translations.inspector.instrument.undefined.plain-som: {$START_TAG_CODE}@{$WRITTEN}{$CLOSE_TAG_CODE} is a custom instrument, but this song defines {$DEFINED}, so the highest is {$START_TAG_CODE}@{$HIGHEST}{$CLOSE_TAG_CODE}.
translations.inspector.instrument.under-am4-a-custom-: {$drums} Under #am4 a custom instrument is written from $13.
translations.inspector.instrument.which-this-song-doe: @{$selected}, which this song does not define
translations.inspector.note-length.sounds-for-of-then: Sounds for {$sounds} of {$span} {$under} ({$percent}%), then {$silence} of silence
translations.inspector.note-length.the-standing-l-is-: the standing `l` is not a length that can be written as `1/n`
translations.inspector.note-length.the-ticks-the-temp: the {$ticks} ticks the tempo ratio leaves it
translations.inspector.note-length.this-note-takes-it: This note takes its length from the standing `l`. Moving the slider writes the length onto the note itself.
translations.inspector.note-length.written-as-an-exac: written as an exact tick count, which is not a note value
translations.inspector.note-palette.add-command.title: Add a command in front of this note
translations.inspector.note-palette.everything-here-i: Everything here is already on this note.
translations.inspector.note-palette.hover-over-a-comm: Hover over a command to see what it does.
translations.inspector.note-picker.octave.label: Octave
translations.inspector.note.nothing-carries-in-from-a: Nothing carries in from an earlier note.
translations.inspector.note.plays-times-showing-pass-: plays {$length} times — showing pass {$pass}, at tick {$tick}
translations.inspector.note.the-commands-acting-on-a: The commands acting on a note are read off the compiled song, so they appear once it compiles.
translations.inspector.pan.addmusick-accepts-2-here-b: AddmusicK accepts 2 here, but the bit it would set is shifted off the byte, so it reads as off.
translations.inspector.pan.bit-5-is-set-which: Bit 5 is set, which the driver reads as neither pan nor surround.
translations.inspector.pan.both-extra-arguments-are-w: Both extra arguments are written or neither. They compile to bits 7 and 6 of a $DB byte.
translations.inspector.pan.needs-a-pan-value: Needs a pan value, as in {$START_TAG_CODE}y10{$CLOSE_TAG_CODE} or {$START_TAG_CODE}$DB $0A{$CLOSE_TAG_CODE}.
translations.inspector.pan.one-byte-the-low-five: One byte: the low five bits are the pan, bit 7 mirrors the left speaker and bit 6 the right. Written as y, that is y<pan>,<left>,<right>.
translations.inspector.pan.pan.label: Pan
translations.inspector.pan.past-the-drivers-21-entry: past the driver's 21-entry pan table, which ends at $14
translations.inspector.pan.surround-left.label: Surround, left
translations.inspector.pan.surround-right.label: Surround, right
translations.inspector.param-table.and-further-argume: {VAR_PLURAL, plural, =1 {… and 1 further argument not shown.} other {… and {COUNT} further arguments not shown.}}
translations.inspector.param-table.carries-shown-in-t: {VAR_PLURAL, plural, =1 {Carries 1 {NOUN}, shown in the hex dump below.} other {Carries {COUNT} {NOUN}s, shown in the hex dump below.}}
translations.inspector.param.addmusic-4-05-overloaded: Addmusic 4.05 overloaded $E5: a high first byte is a sample load, and AddmusicK compiles it to $F3.
translations.inspector.param.addmusic-4-05-wrote-dsp: Addmusic 4.05 wrote DSP registers through $ED. AddmusicK compiles this to $F6.
translations.inspector.param.addmusic-4-05s-tune-comm: Addmusic 4.05’s tune command. AddmusicK compiles this to $FA $02.
translations.inspector.param.amk0163-this-form-was-ne: AMK0163 — this form was never implemented.
translations.inspector.param.an-aram-upload-the-two: An ARAM upload: the two count bytes decide how many of the bytes after it belong to this command.
translations.inspector.param.anything-but-00-selects-: anything but $00 selects the N-SPC table; the driver only tests for zero
translations.inspector.param.c7-multiplies-the-newest: C7 multiplies the newest sample and C0 the oldest.
translations.inspector.param.changes-the-sample-and-c: Changes the sample and coarse pitch only: the envelope and the fractional tuning are left as the previous instrument set them. $FA $FE’s third bit makes $F3 zero the fraction instead.
translations.inspector.param.closes-the-subloop-opene: Closes the subloop opened by the nearest earlier $E6 $00.
translations.inspector.param.each-repeat-is-this-frac: each repeat is this fraction of the last
translations.inspector.param.fades-to-the-amplitude-t: Fades to the amplitude the last $DE set.
translations.inspector.param.inserted-by-the-compiler: Inserted by the compiler at the start of every song; there is rarely a reason to write it by hand.
translations.inspector.param.is-out-of-range-the: ${$byte} is out of range; the driver masks it to ${$masked}
translations.inspector.param.its-handler-has-the-same: Its handler has the same carry-less add as $E2, so a target of $FF fades the song to a stop.
translations.inspector.param.l-nn-writes-an-exact: l=NN writes an exact tick count instead, and dots are allowed — both need #amk 4.
translations.inspector.param.ms-kib-of-aram-reserved: {$ms} ms — {$kib} KiB of ARAM reserved for the buffer
translations.inspector.param.negative-so-this-side-is: negative, so this side is phase-inverted
translations.inspector.param.no-fade-the-driver-skips: no fade — the driver skips a duration of 0, so the value stays put; 1 is what applies it at once
translations.inspector.param.no-feedback-the-echo-pla: no feedback — the echo plays once
translations.inspector.param.no-such-event-the-code: no such event: the code is stored and never run
translations.inspector.param.opens-a-subloop-the-matc: Opens a subloop. The matching $E6 with a non-zero count closes it.
translations.inspector.param.out-of-range-so-the: out of range, so the standing length is kept
translations.inspector.param.past-the-drivers-21-entr: past the driver's 21-entry pan table, which ends at $14
translations.inspector.param.past-the-table-the-spc: past the table: the SPC jumps into whatever follows it
translations.inspector.param.plays-the-subloop-times-: plays the subloop {$count} times — the byte is one less than the count
translations.inspector.param.rate-zero.tremolo: a rate of 0 never advances, so the tremolo stays still
translations.inspector.param.rate-zero.vibrato: a rate of 0 never advances, so the vibrato stays still
translations.inspector.param.replaced-by-remote-code-: replaced by remote code type 3; the slot is empty and the SPC jumps to address zero
translations.inspector.param.replaces-the-instruments: Replaces the instrument’s sample with noise until the next instrument change. The value of the latest n-command being played takes precedence.
translations.inspector.param.sample-the-high-bit-is: sample ${$sample} — the high bit is what selects this form
translations.inspector.param.stops-at-254-the-driver: Stops at 254: the driver adds one, so t255 would be tempo 0 and the song would freeze.
translations.inspector.param.the-address-is-written-b: The address is written by the compiler from a (!n) label; editing it by hand points the driver at nothing.
translations.inspector.param.the-comma-form-needs-amk: The comma form needs #amk 4, so only the first number takes effect here; the rest is read as stray characters.
translations.inspector.param.the-compiler-already-wri: The compiler already writes $FA $06 $01 at the start of every #amk 2 and up song.
translations.inspector.param.the-driver-stores-one-mo: The driver stores one more than you write, so $FF would be tempo 0 and the song would stop advancing.
translations.inspector.param.the-drivers-20th-slot-re: the driver’s 20th slot, reachable only this way — but its sample is dropped as unused, so it plays silence unless the song also uses @21 or @26–@29
translations.inspector.param.the-high-bit-defines-a: the high bit defines a further byte of bits
translations.inspector.param.the-two-bytes-land-on: The two bytes land on the SNES’s APU ports the other way round from how they are written, and stay there until another $F9 changes them. What the ROM does with them is its own business. $F4 $05 reuses the same two bytes as a tick counter, so the two commands cannot both be used.
translations.inspector.param.the-whole-part-only-the: ×{$multiplier} — the whole part only; the fraction carries over from the last instrument
translations.inspector.param.this-driver-has-no-such: this driver has no such command: the SPC jumps to address zero
translations.inspector.param.under-amk-1-this-is: Under #amk 1 this is remote gain, which the compiler rebuilds into a five-byte remote-code event.
translations.inspector.param.volume-1-ff-is-just: volume × {$factor} + 1 — $FF is just shy of double
translations.inspector.param.with-two-arguments-the-f: With two arguments the first is the rate. Add a third and the first becomes a delay instead.
translations.inspector.param.written-by-the-compiler-: Written by the compiler from a [ ] loop. The readme says outright: do not use manually.
translations.inspector.put-the-cursor-on: Put the cursor on a note or command (e.g. {$START_TAG_CODE}$F5{$CLOSE_TAG_CODE}, {$START_TAG_CODE}t{$CLOSE_TAG_CODE}) to see what it does.
translations.inspector.quantization.needs-a-two-digit: Needs a two-digit hex value, as in {$START_TAG_CODE}q7F{$CLOSE_TAG_CODE}.
translations.inspector.quantization.note-length.label: Note length
translations.inspector.quantization.of-a-note-sounds-: of a note sounds — of its last {$piece} ticks, once it is {$long} or longer — and never closer than {$wait} ticks to its end
translations.inspector.quantization.q-must-be-between: q must be between $01 and $7F; ${$byte} is an error at compile time
translations.inspector.quantization.velocity.label: Velocity
translations.inspector.remote-code.cancels.label: Cancels
translations.inspector.remote-code.no-remote-code-is-: No remote code (!{$label}) is defined above the first channel, so this runs nothing.
translations.inspector.remote-code.remote-code-0-can-: Remote code (!0) can never be called: AddmusicK only records a remote body numbered from 1, so this runs nothing. Number the body from 1.
translations.inspector.remote-code.type-runs-no-code-: Type {$type} runs no code, so the (!{$label}) it names is not used.
translations.inspector.remote-code.type.label: Type
translations.inspector.remote-code.wait.label: Wait
translations.inspector.remote.cancel-all-but-the-key: cancel all but the key-on code
translations.inspector.remote.cancels-this-channels-k: Cancels this channel's key-on code. Nothing is run.
translations.inspector.remote.cancels-this-channels-r: Cancels this channel's remote code, the key-on kind included. Nothing is run.
Cancels this channel's remote code except the key-on kind. Nothing is run.
translations.inspector.remote.no-such-type-the-code: No such type: the code is stored and never run, but it replaces a running type 1, 2, 3 or 5.
translations.inspector.remote.reserved-a-key-on-slot: reserved; a key-on slot that fires at key-off
translations.inspector.remote.reserved-stored-as-key-: Reserved. Stored as key-on code, and run at key-off like type 3.
translations.inspector.remote.reserved-the-driver-han: Reserved. The driver handles it exactly as type 2.
translations.inspector.remote.run-on-key-off-instead: run on key-off, instead of the note cut
translations.inspector.remote.run-on-key-on-alongside: run on key-on, alongside the rest
translations.inspector.remote.runs-the-code-as-each: Runs the code as each note keys on, before it sounds. It can run alongside any other type.
translations.inspector.remote.runs-the-code-once-here: Runs the code once, here, alongside whatever else is set.
translations.inspector.remote.runs-the-code-this-long: Runs the code this long after each note keys on. Ties and rests do not count, and a wait longer than the note never fires.
Runs the code this long before each note is cut, which its q decides.
translations.inspector.remote.runs-the-code-where-eac: Runs the code where each note would be cut, and the note keeps sounding until the next one.
translations.inspector.runaway.stopped: playback automatically stopped to protect your ears and speakers due to a runaway {$what}
translations.inspector.the-cursor-is-on: The cursor is on a loop, which is not a command. The {$START_TAG_SPAN}Loop{$CLOSE_TAG_SPAN} panel under this has what it repeats.
translations.inspector.this-command-is-missing: This command is missing arguments, so what it does cannot be read off yet.
translations.inspector.vibrato-graph.no-wobble-a-rate: no wobble — a rate of 0 never advances
translations.inspector.vibrato.a-rate-of-0-never: a rate of 0 never advances, so nothing wobbles
translations.inspector.vibrato.delay.label: Delay
translations.inspector.vibrato.depth.label: Depth
translations.inspector.vibrato.higher-is-faster-one-c: higher is faster — one cycle every {$amount} ticks
translations.inspector.vibrato.needs-a-rate-and: Needs a rate and a depth, and optionally a delay before them.
translations.inspector.vibrato.rate.label: Rate
translations.inspector.vibrato.written-with-two-argum: Written with two arguments, so there is no delay. Add a third and the first becomes one.
translations.inspector.written-as-the-replacement: Written as the {$START_TAG_CODE}"{$REPLACEMENT}"{$CLOSE_TAG_CODE} replacement, so the cursor is on the macro's name rather than on the command itself.
translations.loops.a-body-with-no-name: A body with no name can only be replayed by a *, which names nothing a piano roll can point at.
translations.loops.a-loop-count-must-be: A loop count must be between 1 and 255 (AMK0116).
translations.loops.a-remote-code-definition-cannot: A remote code definition cannot repeat (AMK0164). Its body runs where a (!n, …) call fires it.
translations.loops.a-replays-whichever-loop-was: A * replays whichever loop was opened above it. Naming one writes a (n) call in its place.
translations.loops.a-subloop-cannot-repeat-only: A subloop cannot repeat only once (AMK0126).
translations.loops.a-subloop-must-be-given: A subloop must be given a count (AMK0128).
translations.loops.named-so-a-n-call: Named ({$label}), so a ({$label})n call replays this body from anywhere below it.
translations.loops.no-loop-with-this-number: no loop with this number is declared above here
translations.loops.nothing-is-written-and-a: nothing is written, and a subloop must be given a count
translations.loops.nothing-is-written-and-a-2: {$times} — nothing is written, and a missing count reads as 1
translations.loops.only-loops-declared-above-this: Only loops declared above this call — AddmusicK reads a song in order (AMK0115).
translations.loops.past-256-the-count-wraps: Past 256 the count wraps: the driver is given one less than it, through a byte.
translations.loops.recalls.label: Recalls
translations.loops.repeats.label: Repeats
translations.loops.the-byte-is-one-less: {$times} — the byte is one less than the count

translations.palette.a-loop-and-a-subloop: A loop and a subloop is as deep as AddmusicK goes.
translations.palette.a-loop-cannot-be-called: A loop cannot be called from inside another loop (AMK0112).
translations.palette.a-steady-wobble-in-volume: A steady wobble in volume. The channel's volume pulses.
translations.palette.addmusicms-command-for-writing-a: AddmusicM's command for writing a byte anywhere in the driver's memory.
translations.palette.adds-a-reverb-effect-for: Adds a reverb effect for the specified channels, and how loud it is.
translations.palette.arms-a-remote-snippet-from: Arms a remote snippet from here on, and says what should set it off.
translations.palette.availability.addmusicms-fa-is-no: AddmusicM's $FA is not implemented in AddmusicK (AMK0156).
translations.palette.availability.fc-errors-on-addmus: $FC errors on AddmusicK 1.0.8 and lower, which replaced it with remote code in #amk 2 (AMK0211).
translations.palette.availability.is-not-native-to-ad: ${$vcmd} is not native to Addmusic 4.05; AddmusicK warns (AMK0207).
${$vcmd} is not native to AddmusicM; AddmusicK warns (AMK0207).
translations.palette.availability.the-h-command-is-no: The "h" command is not native to Addmusic 4.05; AddmusicK warns (AMK0205).
translations.palette.availability.written-by-the-comp: Written by the compiler from a [ ] loop. The readme says outright: do not use manually.
Written by the compiler from a (!n) remote call. Prefer (!n) unless you mean the raw bytes.
translations.palette.cancels-a-remote-snippet-so: Cancels a remote snippet so it stops firing.
translations.palette.cycles-quickly-through-a-set: Cycles quickly through a set of notes.
translations.palette.dialect.assumed.title: No #amk, #am4 or #amm marker anywhere in the song, so the palette assumes what the parser assumes. AddmusicK itself rejects a song with no marker (AMK0002).
translations.palette.dialect.marked.title: The dialect this song compiles as. A marker anywhere in the file sets it, and the palette follows it.
translations.palette.drives-the-notes-loudness-direct: Drives the note's loudness directly instead, holding or sliding it to a level.
translations.palette.drops-everything-after-it-by: Drops everything after it by one octave. Compile-time command.
translations.palette.eases-the-vibrato-in-or: Eases the vibrato in or out instead of switching it on at full depth. Must be used after a vibrato (`p`) command.
translations.palette.eight-settings-that-each-take: Eight settings that each take a value: pitch modulation, GAIN, tuning, amplify, echo buffer size.
translations.palette.fades-the-echo-to-the: Fades the echo to the specified volume over time.
translations.palette.hover-over-a-command: Hover over a command to see what it does.
translations.palette.how-a-note-swells-and: How a note swells and dies away: attack, decay, sustain, release.
translations.palette.how-far-behind-the-echo: How far behind the echo sits, how much of it feeds back, and which filter shapes it.
translations.palette.how-loud-the-whole-song: How loud the whole song plays, affects every channel.
translations.palette.how-much-of-each-note: How much of each note actually sounds before it is cut short.
translations.palette.inside-a-loop-this-makes: Inside a loop this makes a subloop - a repeat within the repeat.
translations.palette.inside-a-subloop-this-makes: Inside a subloop this makes an ordinary loop, which is what fits there.
translations.palette.lifts-everything-after-it-by: Lifts everything after it by one octave. Compile-time command.
translations.palette.nine-on-off-switches-legato: Nine on/off switches: legato, light staccato, echo for this channel, Yoshi drums and more.
translations.palette.no-named-loop-is-written: No named loop is written above the cursor. Loops made here name themselves.
translations.palette.nudges-the-pitch-by-a: Nudges the pitch by a fraction of a semitone, applies to the current channel only.
translations.palette.plays-a-loop-you-have: Plays a loop you have already written, again from here.
translations.palette.remote-code-has-to-be: Remote code has to be defined above the first channel; written inside one it is read as a call instead.
translations.palette.repeats-the-notes-you-have: Repeats the notes you have selected.
translations.palette.repeats-the-selected-notes-insid: Repeats the selected notes inside a repeat that is already running.
translations.palette.select-the-notes-the-loop: Select the notes the loop should play.
translations.palette.sends-two-bytes-to-the: Sends two bytes to the SNES for the ROM to read. Changes nothing you can hear.
translations.palette.set-the-channels-sound-position: Set the channel's sound position between the left and right speaker.
translations.palette.sets-the-default-note-length: Sets the default note length as an exact number of ticks. Compile-time command.
translations.palette.shapes-the-tone-of-the: Shapes the tone of the echo by selectively reducing or emphasizing frequencies. It affects how bright or muffled the repeats sound.
translations.palette.shifts-every-note-written-after: Shifts every note written after it up or down by a number of semitones. Compile-time command.
translations.palette.shifts-the-pitch-up-or: Shifts the pitch up or down by a number of semitones. Applies to the entire song.

translations.sst.0501: The echo feedback at ${$feedback} and filter {$filter} make the echo grow instead of fade, so the song will get loud and distorted. Lower the feedback.
translations.sst.0501.filter-zero: The echo feedback at ${$feedback} and filter 0 make the echo grow instead of fade, so the song will get loud and distorted. Lower the feedback, or select filter 1.
translations.sst.0502.one: {$channel} is longer than the song. It lasts as long as its shortest channel, #{$shortest} at {$ticks} ticks, and everything past that is never played.
translations.sst.0502.other: {$channels} are longer than the song. It lasts as long as its shortest channel, #{$shortest} at {$ticks} ticks, and everything past that is never played.
translations.sst.0503: The driver cannot keep up with this song's tempo: it plays about {$percent}% slower than written. Lower the tempo, or give the busiest channels less to do.
translations.sst.0504: #path does nothing here, as Solar Soundtrack's sample library is one flat folder. AddmusicK itself still accepts this directive.
translations.sst.0505: Replacement "{$name}" is expanding without end. A replacement whose value contains its own name, directly or through another replacement, grows the song faster than it is read; AddmusicK does not stop either.
translations.sst.0506: $F7 was never implemented in this driver: its dispatch slot is $0000, so the SPC jumps to address zero and the song stops. Remove the command.
translations.sst.0507.blocked: The {$command} written between this $DD and the note before it is what the driver reads instead — the read-ahead only ever looks at the very next byte — so the $DD runs as a command, jumps to address zero and the song stops. Move it to directly after the note.
translations.sst.0507.note-one-tick: The note before this $DD lasts one tick, and the read-ahead cannot run on the tick a note begins, so the $DD runs as a command, jumps to address zero and the song stops. Give that note two ticks or more.
translations.sst.0507.note-pieces: The note before this $DD is {$ticks} ticks, which the compiler writes in pieces of 96 with one tick left over at the end, and the read-ahead cannot run on the tick a piece begins, so the $DD runs as a command, jumps to address zero and the song stops. Make that note a tick longer or shorter.
translations.sst.0507.nothing: No note plays before this $DD on the channel, so the $DD runs as a command, jumps to address zero and the song stops. Write it directly after a note of two ticks or more.
translations.sst.0507.tie-one-tick: The tie before this $DD lasts one tick, and the read-ahead cannot run on the tick a tie begins, so the $DD runs as a command, jumps to address zero and the song stops. Give that tie two ticks or more.
translations.sst.0507.tie-pieces: The tie before this $DD is {$ticks} ticks, which the compiler writes in pieces of 96 with one tick left over at the end, and the read-ahead cannot run on the tick a piece begins, so the $DD runs as a command, jumps to address zero and the song stops. Make that tie a tick longer or shorter.
translations.sst.0508: Under #am4, the compiler adds one to this transpose, so it lands a semitone above what is written. Double check to write one less than you want.
translations.sst.0509: No remote code (!{$label}) is defined above the first channel, so this event runs nothing. AddmusicK compiles it without a word.
translations.sst.0509.zero: Remote code (!0) can never be called: AddmusicK only records the address of a remote body numbered from 1, so this event runs nothing. Number the body from 1.

translations.sst.0511.default: This {$command} carries over into the song's repeat, where #{$channel}'s loop starts under it instead of as the song starts. Set it back on #{$channel} before the first note or rest after the /, or before its first note or rest if there is no /.
